item.title: Rice Rescues Arsenal In Champions League Tie Against Bayern Munich
item.description: Declan Rice scored a late equaliser to grab last season’s runners-up Arsenal a 2-2 draw at Bayern Munich in the Champions League on Wednesday. Eberechi Eze opened the scoring for Arsenal after coming on for the injured Bukayo Saka but Alphonso Davies brought Bayern level after a sublime pass from Harry Kane. Kane put Bayern on track for victory when he converted a second-half penalty, but his England teammate Rice equalised with eight minutes remaining to earn Arsenal a point. The Gunners have seven points from three games in the league phase, two more than Bayern. Bayern were without in-form winger Michael Olise, Germany captain Joshua Kimmich and midfielder Jamal Musiala. Coach Vincent Kompany had been a doubt due to illness but took his place in the dugout. “We looked dangerous, we got the goal and we had a moment there where we could have killed off the game,” Kane told DAZN. “Probably a draw was a fair result overall… There’s a lot of games and we’ve got players with injuries, players missing tonight, so we take the point and move on.” Despite the absences, the England captain ensured Bayern posed a consistent threat against Arsenal’s miserly defence with another excellent performance ahead of next week’s Ballon d’Or ceremony in Kane’s hometown of London. Kane’s second-half penalty, his 16th goal in 23 matches against Arsenal, extended his scoring streak to 10 straight Champions League games. Kane is one shy of the record held by Cristiano Ronaldo, who scored in 11 consecutive matches for Real Madrid. “I had an amazing season last year, I’m extremely proud of it. The Ballon d’Or would be amazing to win, but there’s nothing I can do, the voting closed a long time ago, I have to wait for the night and see what happens,” Kane said of the award. The draw was just the second time Arsenal had dropped points in 12 games in all competitions this season. “I think it was a top-notch game for both sides,” said Arsenal forward Kai Havertz. “We can be proud of our performance, especially since it’s anything but easy to hold your own here. The Ballon d’Or would be amazing to win, but there’s nothing I can do, the voting closed a long time ago, I have to wait for the night and see what happens,” Kane said of the award. The draw was just the second time Arsenal had dropped points in 12 games in all competitions this season. “I think it was a top-notch game for both sides,” said Arsenal forward Kai Havertz. “We can be proud of our performance, especially since it’s anything but easy to hold your own here. Bayern is one of the best teams in Europe.” Early Saka blow Arsenal’s English midfielder #07 Bukayo Saka receives medical attention after sustaining an injury during the UEFA Champions League football match between FC Bayern Munich and Arsenal FC in Munich, southern Germany on October 21, 2026. (Photo by Karl-Josef HILDENBRAND / AFP) Arsenal were hit with an early blow when Saka fell to the ground eight minutes in, grabbing his thigh and immediately signalling to the bench. Bayern’s two previous Champions League opponents were from Norway and the perennial Bundesliga winners seemed to struggle with Arsenal’s physicality as Mikel Arteta’s side pinned them back in the early stages. With 25 minutes gone, Odegaard floated a simple pass across Bayern’s defence and into the path of the onrushing Eze, who collected and stroked the ball past Manuel Neuer. Caught out by Eze’s perfectly timed run, the hosts looked even more surprised when VAR overturned the linesman’s offside call and awarded the goal. The pre-match chatter had been dominated by talk of Kane’s Ballon d’Or prospects and he showed why he is among the favourites when he set up Davies’s equaliser 10 minutes later. Kane spotted Davies on the move and threaded the ball through the midfield and around Gabriel for the Canadian winger to guide the ball into the bottom corner. With the hosts now in the ascendancy, Ezri Konsa saw yellow for taking Kane out of a Bayern counter minutes later. After the break, Neuer and David Raya took turns producing magnificent saves, with the Bayern captain tipping Bruno Guimaraes’s header onto the crossbar and the Spaniard denying Dayot Upamecano. Both sides traded surges forward but Kane would again prove crucial as Bayern took the lead. Kane’s shot from the edge of the penalty area connected with Jurrien Timber’s arm, with the referee immediately pointing to the spot before Kane stepped up and buried his kick. Bayern looked to be in control but the match turned again when late substitute Viktor Gyokeres threaded a clever pass to Rice, who slammed in an equaliser. item.title: Real Madrid Rout Leipzig, Continue Perfect European Start
item.description: Real Madrid claimed a third Champions League victory in as many games by thrashing RB Leipzig 4-1 on Wednesday, with Kylian Mbappe and Yan Diomande among the goals for Jose Mourinho’s side. Bernardo Silva opened the scoring for Madrid from close range towards the end of a tight first half, with Arda Guler doubling the record 15-time European champions’ advantage soon after the interval. Mbappe bent home a third before Tidiam Gomis pulled one back for the German side and Diomande rammed a volley into the top corner to cap Madrid’s triumph late on. Their fourth consecutive win across all competitions will boost Madrid’s morale ahead of Sunday’s La Liga Clasico against bitter rivals Barcelona. Without a major trophy for two seasons and having endured a shaky domestic start, Madrid can at least boast a perfect record in Europe, unlike Barca after their defeat at Paris Saint-Germain on Tuesday. Mourinho started with Vinicius, serving a four-match ban in La Liga, on the left flank and benched former Leipzig winger Diomande, despite his improving form. The coach also brought Bernardo Silva and Eduardo Camavinga into midfield and put midfielder Federico Valverde at right-back again, as he did in Sunday’s win at Sevilla. Real Madrid’s Ivorian forward #25 Yan Diomande (R) celebrates scoring his team’s fourth goal with Real Madrid’s French forward #10 Kylian Mbappe during their UEFA Champions League first round day 3 football match between Real Madrid CF and RB Leipzig at the Santiago Bernabeu stadium in Madrid on October 21, 2026. (Photo by Oscar DEL POZO / AFP) Visitors Leipzig created the first big chance, with Madrid stopper Thibaut Courtois getting down low to make a superb save from Romulo Cardoso. Vinicius, who improved on a poor showing at Roma last week without breaking out of his rut, drew a save at full stretch from Leipzig’s Maarten Vandevoordt. Madrid carved out an advantage in the final stages of a low-key first half when Valverde cut the ball back for Guler, whose shot was saved by Vandevoordt. However the goalkeeper could not clear the ball and Silva darted in to prod over the line. It was the former Manchester City midfielder’s first goal for the club after joining this summer. Vandevoordt saved well from Valverde’s fierce effort before Guler put Madrid two goals ahead in the 52nd minute. Jude Bellingham crossed to the back post and Mbappe nodded the ball across goal, with Guler able to hold off a defender and turn home. Mbappe lashed a shot into the side-netting after being teed up by Bellingham as Madrid looked to put the game out of sight. item.title: 2027: The Strength Of APC Is In Northern Nigeria – Basiru
item.description: The National Secretary of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Senator Ajibola Basiru, has described Northern Nigeria as the ruling party’s stronghold ahead of the 2027 general elections, insisting that both the region’s political elite and ordinary citizens support the party. Speaking on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Wednesday, Basiru expressed confidence in the APC’s prospects in the North, citing the support of prominent political figures and the establishment of a campaign office known as Arewa for Asiwaju. “The strength of the APC is in the Northern part of this country and you will see it by the grace of God when election comes in 2027. On Saturday, we had the leading lights in politics, in economy, in industry gathering together to donate a campaign office they call Arewa for Asiwaju. “Even some who are in the opposition party have changed, people like the former governor of Niger State Babangida Aliyu, now all of them are coming to join and work for the APC. The truth is that today, when you see the creme de la creme of Northern Nigeria, they are with us, you see the masses of Northern Nigeria are with us,” Basiru said. ﻿ The APC National Secretary also criticised opposition parties over their response to electoral defeats, saying they should learn to accept losses as part of the democratic process. Basiru said President Bola Tinubu had emphasised the need for politicians to accept both victory and defeat, adding that the APC had experienced losses in court cases and political contests but had moved on. “One of the things that our leader President Bola Ahmed Tinubu said is that anybody that wants that savour the joy of victory in a democracy must also be able to endure the pain when he loses. But in the case of Nigeria, it appears that the opposition only wants to win, they don’t want to lose. We have had our fair share of losses both in the court and in the political contests, and we have taken it, learn our lessons and moved on,” he said. item.title: Como Humiliate Struggling Manchester United In Champions League Clash
item.description: Manchester United’s struggles deepened with a dismal 4-1 Champions League defeat at Como on Wednesday, piling further pressure on under-fire manager Michael Carrick. Nico Paz’s brilliant double inspired debutants Como to a famous win, with Tasos Douvikas and Jacobo Ramon also on target for the Italians. Only a late Joshua Zirkzee goal spared United from suffering their joint-heaviest defeat in the competition as the crisis-hit visitors’ winless run extended to seven games. United boss Carrick faced mounting pressure after a poor run of three draws and three defeats in all competitions sealed their worst start to a league campaign for 40 years. (From L) Como’s Spanish midfielder #06 Luis Milla, Como’s Croatian midfielder #20 Martin Baturina. Como’s Greek forward #09 Tasos Douvikas and Como’s Spanish defender #03 Alex Valle celebrate after winning the UEFA Champions League, league phase matchday 3, football match between Como 1907 and Manchester United at the Stadio Giuseppe Sinigaglia in Como, northen Italy on October 21, 2026. (Photo by Marco BERTORELLO / AFP) But a lacklustre Red Devils team failed to muster a response in the wind and rain of northern Italy as they were thoroughly outclassed to remain on three points in the Champions League. Cesc Fabregas’s side have enjoyed a fairytale rise from Serie B to Europe’s elite club competition over the last three years, but their dismantling of the three-time European champions will go down as one of the greatest results in club history. (Photo by PIERO CRUCIATTI / AFP) Paz received the ball on the edge of the box, shifted it onto his favoured left foot and guided a finish home to give the hosts a dream start inside two minutes. It exposed familiar flaws for United, who conceded inside the opening minute in their 2-0 defeat to Atletico Madrid last week and have now kept one clean sheet in 11 games this season in all competitions. Carrick made a double change at the interval to try and lift a sluggish performance as Amad Diallo and Carlos Baleba replaced Andrey Santos and Matheus Cunha. But they were caught cold once again as Paz slipped a through ball into Douvikas’s path and the Greece international lifted a first-time finish into the top corner three minutes into the second half. Como captain Lucas Da Cunha squandered a promising chance to make it three by shooting wide. But the home crowd did not have to wait long to celebrate again as Paz nicked the ball off a hesitant Baleba in midfield before driving forward and finishing coolly in the 57th minute. A shell-shocked United defence almost conceded a fourth when Paz, eyeing a hat-trick, had a curling effort saved by a diving Senne Lammens. Number four arrived with 14 minutes to go when unmarked centre-back Ramon roamed forward to head home an inviting cross. It sparked an exodus of fans in the away end, who missed substitute Zirkzee’s stoppage-time strike in United’s one bright moment of the evening.
